name: Rites of Spring
label: Dischord
lede: Rites of Spring played about fifteen shows, cut one album and left a four-song single in the can. Forty years on, the band still gets credited with a genre name it never used.

eras.title: Hardcore with the macho pose removed
eras.text: By 1983 D.C. hardcore had grown bigger, meaner and more predictable, and plenty of the kids who built it were bored. Three veterans of Insurrection, joined by Eddie Janney from Faith, kept the speed and dropped the posturing.

years.h: Insurrection alumni start writing as Rites of Spring
years.p: [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]], [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] and [[Mike Fellows|58a7226f-e06a-4728-82a5-ddc4443025a4]] had played hardcore together in Insurrection. By December they have the first songs: "All There Is", "End on End", "By Design".

years.h: A name borrowed from a Stravinsky riot
years.p: The Rite of Spring is the ballet whose 1913 premiere ended in uproar. Picciotto liked the second meaning too: a spring for a D.C. scene that had gone stale.

years.cap: Flyer for Rites of Spring with King Face and Lunch Meat, Chevy Chase Community Center
years.src: Dischord · Wikipedia: Rites of Spring · WETA Boundary Stones
years.h: First shows, spring 1984, and some broken gear
years.p: Dischord dates the first shows to spring 1984. The band would play only about fifteen in all, and sometimes left the stage with less equipment than it arrived with.
years.xp:
Wikipedia counts 19 shows, 16 in the D.C. area and three outside it. Dischord's count is fifteen. Either way, it's a short run.

WETA's account says core members of the scene were hooked after just two shows, and that the band was known for melodic guitars, lyrics turned inward and wrecking its own instruments.

years.h: Fellows heads to California, the others keep rehearsing
years.p: Bassist Fellows moves west and the rest rehearse without him, figuring he's gone for good. About three months later he's back.

eras.title: Revolution Summer
eras.text: For one season, D.C. punk turned outward and inward at once: benefit shows, protests at the South African Embassy, songs about things hardcore usually shrugged off. Rites of Spring sat in the middle of it, with a record to match.

years.src: Dischord · Wikipedia: Rites of Spring · UMD Libraries, Persistent Vision
yt: "For Want Of" live at the old 9:30 Club, 1985
years.h: Rites of Spring, Dischord No. 16
years.p: Their only album, cut at Inner Ear in February with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] producing. Later reissues tack on the All Through a Life single and retitle it End on End.
years.xp:
Wikipedia counts twelve tracks. The sound is hardcore speed with the anger turned inward: confessional, melodic, about the things punk usually kept quiet. The band pointed to the Smiths, Wire, the Buzzcocks and the Birthday Party, and to Faith's 1983 EP Subject to Change.

The University of Maryland's Persistent Vision exhibit sums it up as taking "the energy and ferocity of hardcore" and adding "a far more melodic songwriting sense."

years.cap: Flyer for the Punk Percussion Protest, June 21, 1985
q: Punk is about building things, not destroying them.
years.src: WETA Boundary Stones · Wikipedia: Revolution Summer (music)
years.h: Rites of Spring announce a drum protest against apartheid
years.p: At the Chevy Chase Community Center, the band uses its stage to announce the first Punk Percussion Protest: punks with drums outside the South African Embassy, making noise against apartheid.
years.xp:
Embassy protests had been running since November 1984, and the punks joined them on June 21, 1985. WETA reports the drumming carried "three or four miles away." That night Rites of Spring played the 9:30 Club, where Picciotto thanked the crowd for showing up.

The band's gear-smashing reputation followed it anyway. At a 9:30 Club show Picciotto pushed back on it from the stage.

years.src: WETA Boundary Stones · Wikipedia: Revolution Summer (music)
years.h: A summer-jobs office names Revolution Summer
years.p: Amy Pickering, who worked at Dischord, and Chris Thomson coined the name at a city office, as an inside joke about revolting against their supervisor. It went on to label a whole season of D.C. bands.
years.xp: Per WETA, the pair made fliers at the Neighborhood Planning Council office that read "Be on your toes. This is Revolution Summer."

years.cap: Flyer for the WGTB benefit, Hall of Nations, Georgetown, December 4, 1985
years.h: "Emocore" gets its first laugh at a Rites of Spring show
years.p: The bill has [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]], Rites of Spring and [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]]. Dag Nasty guitarist [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] says he came up with "emocore" there, to needle the Rites of Spring set. That's his account, told to Parade in 2025.
years.xp:
Baker said he didn't think of it as coining anything at the time. A friend pointed out where the word had come from years later.

Whoever said it first, Rites of Spring never used it about themselves.

years.h: Live at CCCC, Bethesda MD, October 25, 1985
yt: Live at CCCC, Bethesda MD, October 25, 1985

eras.title: Out as fast as they came in
eras.text: The band ended the way it played: quickly, with no speech. One last session in January 1986, a split within weeks, and three of the four in a new band before summer.

years.h: Rites of Spring split, under two years after the first show
years.p: Wikipedia puts the breakup in January 1986, right after the All Through a Life session; Dischord says winter 1986. No member has given a reason on the record.
years.xp: Fifteen shows by Dischord's count (Wikipedia says 19), one LP, and one single still in the can.

years.h: Picciotto, Janney and Canty start One Last Wish
years.p: [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]], [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] and [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] bring in Embrace guitarist [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]]. They play out from August and record an album at Inner Ear in November.

eras.title: Same people, new names
eras.text: Nobody in Rites of Spring was done with anybody else. In eighteen months the members ran through One Last Wish and Happy Go Licky, and then Brendan Canty and Guy Picciotto walked into Fugazi.

years.h: Canty takes the drum stool in Fugazi
years.p: [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] replaces Colin Sears in [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]'s new band, Fugazi.

years.h: One more Rites of Spring record, after the funeral
years.p: The final four songs, cut at Inner Ear in January 1986 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], come out as a 7-inch, All Through a Life, a year after the split.
years.xp: The CD and cassette of the LP that year folded these songs in, plus one more, "Other Way Around."

years.h: The four regroup as Happy Go Licky, and get strange
years.p: Picciotto, Janney, Fellows and Canty are together again, playing tape loops, sound effects and songs largely or entirely improvised. They never set foot in a studio.

years.cap: Guy Picciotto and Ian MacKaye of Fugazi at Dupont Circle
years.h: Picciotto on stage with Fugazi by show two
years.p: He's singing with the band by their second show and joins for good once Happy Go Licky winds down.

years.h: Happy Go Licky close on New Year's Day
years.p: The four-piece play their last show at the 9:30 Club. From here the Rites of Spring story runs through Fugazi.

eras.title: Fugazi fans go digging
eras.text: Fugazi was drawing crowds worldwide, and new listeners went looking for where Picciotto and Canty came from. Dischord put the Rites of Spring recordings on one disc, End on End, and let the side projects out a little at a time.

years.h: End on End puts all of Rites of Spring on one disc
years.p: Seventeen tracks: the LP, the All Through a Life single and "Other Way Around", under the title most fans know. Dischord still files it as No. 16.

years.h: Happy Go Licky finally reach Dischord
years.p: Will Play collects live recordings from the band that never made a studio record.

years.h: One Last Wish's 1986 sits on a shelf until 1999
years.p: The band broke up in January 1987 after mixing the album, and Dischord held it back. It's named for the one year the band existed.
years.xp: The album was recorded in November 1986 by Picciotto, Janney, Canty and Hampton. Dischord was wary of its growing reputation as a home for bands that no longer existed; one track slipped out on a 1989 benefit compilation.

eras.title: The word they never asked for
eras.text: By the 2000s emo was on magazine covers, and Rites of Spring kept getting named as the place it started. The band wanted no part of it. Meanwhile the vault gave up the very first tape.

years.h: Mike Fellows releases a self-titled record as Miighty Flashlight
years.p: After years of session work around the Drag City label, the former Rites of Spring bassist puts out an album under that name.

years.big: "Rites of Spring existed well before the term did."
q: I've never recognized 'emo' as a genre of music.
years.h: Picciotto won't have the emo label
years.p: Asked about Rites of Spring being called the first emo band, Guy Picciotto refuses the premise. The line in the big type is [[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]]'s.
years.xp:
In a 2003 interview Picciotto said he'd never recognized "emo" as a genre, and called it "the most retarded term ever." Every band he'd played in, he said, was simply a punk rock band. His counterexample: nobody would say Bad Brains weren't emotional.

Toomey's full line: they existed well before the term did, "and they hated it."

years.h: Eddie Vedder lists them among his influences
years.p: Rites of Spring had fans well outside hardcore. Wikipedia notes Pearl Jam singer [[Eddie Vedder|1a60d6dd-9d3e-40fc-a66d-3184f9ee0d61]] has cited them.

years.h: Six Song Demo turns up 28 years late
years.p: The first session, cut at Inner Ear in April 1984 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing and [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] new on second guitar, sat unreleased until Dischord No. 176 put it on 10-inch vinyl and download.
years.xp: The tape holds "End on End", "All There Is" and "By Design", the first songs the band wrote, in their first recorded form.
